name: POST /api/leadflow/contacts/:id/properties/link - a contextual role
description:
Links a property to a person as a CONTEXTUAL ROLE.

THE ADDRESS IS CANONICALISED UPSTREAM before the relationship is written, which is why this takes a raw address rather than an id — resolving it in the browser would let the client decide which place a string means, and two operators typing the same house differently would create two properties. An unresolvable address REFUSES rather than linking against the raw string.

NO PROPERTY FACT IS WRITTEN ONTO THE PERSON, and person_attributes_written: 0 is returned as proof rather than as a promise. A role is a relationship between a person and a place; copying "owns 14 Elm St" onto the person record is how it survives the sale of the house.

Evidence and a start date are mandatory: a role with neither is an assertion nobody can date or defend.

QA NOTE: sdk-geo is not configured in this environment, so the canonicalisation refusal is the path under test. That refusal IS the guarantee — linking against a raw address string would create a second property for the same place the next time somebody types it differently, and a duplicate property is not recoverable by editing.

testCases.name: Linking is REFUSED when the address cannot be canonicalised
A link with no evidence and no start date is REFUSED
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: trust_state, valid_from, evidence_type are required - a role with no evidence and no start date is an assertion nobody can date or defend
errorCases.when: any of address, role, trust_state, valid_from or evidence_type is missing.

errorCases.message: The address could not be canonicalised, so no relationship was written. Linking against a raw string would create a second property for the same place the next time somebody types it differently.
errorCases.when: the geo service cannot resolve the address. Refusing is deliberate — a duplicate property is not recoverable by editing.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
